A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMO Sampler work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. v1 Appendix B corresponds to v2 Appendix A.6; the retained material and additions can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations, image-generation experiments, ablations, and human evaluations, including comparisons on SD3, Flux, and AuraFlow.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds anatomy-rendering examples, specialized models' OCR scores, and a manual OCR-recognition audit.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.1-3.3 retain the same ODE overshooting, noise compensation, and attention modulation. The new appendix applications do not document a changed sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix A.7 and Figure 14 add anatomy-focused scenarios: a hand gripping a cliff and a yoga class with ten participants. The existing text-rendering datasets and model coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds TextDiffuser and GlyphControl to the quantitative OCR-A/OCR-F comparison with Flux-Euler and Flux-AMO. Both specialized models already appeared in v1's human and qualitative comparisons, so this is a limited expansion of their comparison role.

E3.justification: Appendix A.8 newly reports a manual audit of OCR recognition using 500 TMDBEval500 images, extending v1's qualitative OCR-failure analysis. The original benchmark metrics, sampling budgets, model configurations, and human-study settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds hand/body-rendering case studies in Figure 14 and a quantitative assessment of OCR recognition failures in A.8. The component ablations, overshooting-strength analysis, and earlier qualitative error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Run/seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. The added OCR scores and audit percentages introduce no confidence intervals, significance tests, or reported repeated-run procedures.

E6.justification: The existing results remain unchanged. Table 5 newly reports OCR-A/OCR-F scores of 0.491/0.625 for TextDiffuser and 0.537/0.591 for GlyphControl, alongside retained Flux scores. A.8 adds OCR-recognition accuracy of 54% for Flux versus 92% for TextDiffuser, and Figure 14 adds qualitative anatomy results.

T1.justification: The sampling equations, SDE-limit derivation, and Lemmas A.1 and A.2 with their proofs are unchanged. Moving a footnote into the prose does not alter the mathematical assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free text-rendering contribution, negligible-overhead claim, and stated 32.3%/35.9% improvements. The new anatomy examples remain exploratory appendix material.

C2.justification: A.7 discusses possible benefits for hand/body rendering while acknowledging the difficulty of quantifying them without extensive human evaluation. A.8 interprets the new OCR rankings through font/style bias, extending an OCR limitation already discussed in v1 A.4.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit AMO code-repository link in the abstract. The hardware, model precision, hyperparameters, and existing evaluation instructions in Section 5 and Appendix A.3 are retained.

R1.justification: The same 35 cited works and the related-work positioning in Section 4 are retained. Reference back-page updates and the added acknowledgments do not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and short Appendices A.7-A.8, renumbers Appendix B as A.6, and incorporates a footnote into the prose. Most wording and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 14 and Table 5, relocates Table 2 from PDF page 7 to page 6, and makes associated layout adjustments. The existing figures and tables are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves evidential transparency by reporting specialized models' OCR scores and quantifying OCR-recognition failures, making the existing evaluation caveat more assessable. The code-access link improves reproducibility information. The anatomy examples remain qualitative, and the core method and main results are unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
